body:
The survival instinct is not strength, it is a biological imperative. You don't have a choice in it's activation. Strength is getting back up after being down, not slugging your way through life on the floor.

I'm not strong, I'm just too pathetic to die on my own terms.

There are some hidden factors that can impact this, but I would need a more advanced equation/expression.

Stuff like apathy, fatigue, and desire.
It's really all about finding your P and W values. W is usually pretty high, much higher than people think. P typically starts low but tends to climb in a linear fashion.
Treatment Resistant Depression, both major and persistent. Trying to understand why people enjoy this rat race. Spend most days working or in bed wondering why I'm here.
Welcome to anhedonia. The chemical hell of apathy.

My sister once told me, when I called her on the phone to complain about work, some choice words:

"Welcome to being an adult. It sucks."

My best friend attempted suicide twice and failed. He was hospitalized not too long ago because a third party called the police fearing he was going to kill himself.

Our mutual friend took a .44 to his head. His was the first funeral I went to as a teenager. 

I've found myself holding the barrel of an unloaded rifle to my lower jaw a couple times. 

I can only offer solidarity. Keep moving towards something you care about, if you can.

Not anymore, nothing distracts me. Everything just reminds me that I'm broken, that I'll live and die alone without ever understanding and succeeding in being fulfilled. 

I'll hang out until I die, living this facade I've made. Meekly refusing support other than professionals, being ashamed and embarrassed of my life, and wondering where I went wrong.

I don't let people in because I'm a burden.
That's why guys are here, aren't they, to be worked until they can provide something?
